newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Qantas and Ansett Australia are set to tighten restrictions on discount fare deals to combat an unexpected change in the domestic airline market which has seen up to 40 per cent of business travellers flying on cut-price leisure-based tickets. The airlines say they need to take action to protect their revenue streams and yields. Page 1.

The Governor of the Reserve Bank, Ian Macfarlane, has expressed growing concern about a possible deterioration in the quality of corporate loans. Speaking at the Reserve Bank's regular six-monthly meeting with international banks operating in Australia, Macfarlane also highlighted the problem of local and overseas banks offering cheap loans with lenient terms. Page 1.

A survey by investment consultants AT Kearney has shown that Australia's managers delivered a A$23 billion profit in capital gains to shareholders last year but that the return on equity from 50 per cent of big companies was less than that five years ago. Furthermore, in dollar terms, total corporate profitability outside the banking industry is over A$500 million lower this year than in the recession of 1991. Page 1.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, Australia's largest magazine and television company, is set to sign a joint venture deal with Microsoft for the latter's Internet content in the South Pacific. PBL's Internet arm, PBL Online and Microsoft wll form a new jointly owned company which will sell Microsoft's Internet magazines and combine them with PBL's magazine and television content, adapted for the local Internet market. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A Newspoll issues survey has found the electorate does not believe the May Budget has effectively tackled unemployment. This, along with fears about job security, has pushed the Labor Opposition ahead of the Government on this key issue, with the ALP now being regarded as the most effective party on unemployment, leading the Government 33 to 27 per cent. Page 1.

Federal Cabinet is today expected to approve significant new restrictions on the rules for paying unemployment benefits to 18 to 20 year olds and the introduction of rental assistance to 100,000 Austudy recipients. The scheme is expected to be jointly recommended by Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman and Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone. Page 1.

A taped conversation between two policemen following a drug squad raid, in which they joke about the amount of illegal money they will get from the operation, has been broadcast of WA radio and television, and printed in a newspaper. The incident has placed increased pressure on the State's Anti-Corruption Commission to recommend a Royal Commission into the police force. Page 1.

The Australian Council of Social Services has warned Prime Minister John Howard that it would strongly oppose any goods and services tax similar to that offered in the Coalition's 1993 Fightback policy. It also claimed that the Federal Government's preset push for a GST would fail like similar attempts by Paul Keating in 1985 and John Hewson in 1993. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A former prefect at Parramatta West Public School, 18-year-old Rebecca Bernauer is the latest victim of heroin in NSW. She was found dead early Saturday morning, her body dumped in Kings Cross. It is yet to be determined whether she was murdered, or sufered an overdose. Page 1.

The NSW Government has proposed tougher restrictions on the setting up of new private schools in a move aimed to stop the falling enrolments in public schools that are threatening some with closure. Education authorities predict enrolments in private schools will grow from 29.4 per cent to over 31 per cent in 2000. Page 1.

Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer met Frank Gilford, brother of murdered Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, last weekend to discuss the sentencing alternatives to the death penalty, if the two British nurses accused of the murder are found guilty by the Saudi Arabian courts. Page 1.

Figures released by the NSW Department of Health showing general surgery waiting times in regional and rural areas of six weeks to two months have been contradicted by figures from Shoalhaven Hospital in the Illawarra region that show patients can wait up to 22 months for common procedures. Page 2.
THE AGE

Investigations by the Age have revealed that children in orphanages and baby homes in Victoria were used as guinea pigs in post World War II medical experiments and research that continued until 1970. The tests included trails of vaccines that were defective or failed to pass safety tests in animals. Page 1.

Computer expert Steve Outtrim is currently experiencing financial difficulties which have pushed him to the verge of bankruptcy. Outtrim has suffered a series of setbacks following his promising debut last October when he became an instant multi-millionaie with the successful sharemarket debut of his Melbourne-based computer company, Sausage Software. Page 1.

The business and welfare sectors have combined to urge the Federal Government to conduct a broad debate on tax reform, one not restricted to the GST. Recent comments by Federal Government ministers have raised concerns that a broad-based GST is being planned as the cornerstone of any new taxation policy. Page 2.

Australian GeneEthics Network director Bob Phelps has criticised a decision by Melbourne pharmaceutical company AMRAD to patent a mildly retarded child's DNA sequence following the discovery by the Murdoch Institute of Research into Birth Defects of an uusual genetic kink on a chromosome. Page 2.
